purpose: Custom-model electricity briefing endpoint for the existing multi-capability Alexa skill. The Smart Home Lambda stays separate and unchanged.

lambda.architecture: arm64 or x86_64 (pure Python, no native deps)

trigger.skillIdVerification: enabled with the same skill id as ALEXA_SKILL_ID

lambda.iam: Basic execution role only (CloudWatch Logs). No other AWS permissions are used.
lambda.network: Outbound HTTPS to hass.iacob.co.uk only, two read-only GETs per invocation, no retries, TLS verified, redirects refused, 512 KiB body cap, 3 s socket timeout each, 6 s shared budget.

skillManifest.mergeStrategy: Deep-merge manifest-custom-patch.json into the live manifest fetched via SMAPI. Only manifest.apis.custom is added or replaced; manifest.apis.smartHome, manifest.permissions, manifest.privacyAndCompliance and the accountLinking configuration must be left exactly as they are.
skillManifest.accountLinking: Unchanged. The custom API reuses the Home Assistant OAuth link already configured for the skill; the handler reads the token from context.System.user.accessToken (fallback session.user.accessToken).

interactionModel.routineNote: A casual phrase can be mapped with an Alexa Routine that opens this custom model; there is no name-free UK invocation.

homeAssistant.contract: attributes.rates is a list of {start, end, value_inc_vat (GBP/kWh), is_capped}; 30 minute slots with timezone-aware ISO timestamps.

tests.network: none; all HTTP is mocked at lambda_function._perform_get
tests.status: Verified on devbox; see pull request for test counts and live Lambda acceptance.
